decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm mouse approach with gradual elbow-up lift and downward wrist rotation; left remains home.
Advance right wrist above the mouse, maintaining clearance and gradually aligning the open fingers with its sides.
Descend toward mouse with near-vertical fingers; use wrist view next to refine final grasp depth.
Refine mouse grasp by a small forward/down adjustment, close fully, and test retention with a short lift.
Mouse appears retained between fingers. Carry it rightward over the mouse pad with a small clearance lift, keeping the grasp closed.
Lower mouse onto the pad, open the fingers, then lift clear to verify placement.
Mouse rests on pad. Retract right arm and bring both wrists toward keyboard-pushing approach, keeping elbows raised and fingers clear.
Bring closed fingertips behind the keyboard's front edge, with separate left/right contact points for a controlled forward push.
Push the keyboard gradually forward and slightly right toward its outline, monitoring both contact points.
Keyboard did not translate; fingertips were too high. Withdraw, lower behind its front edge, and re-establish contact.
Both fingertips now contact the keyboard front. Push forward with a slight rightward correction while holding the current height.
Keyboard is translating toward its frame. Continue a shorter forward push with increased rightward alignment, without crossing the arms.
Keyboard appears aligned with the frame. Open both grippers and withdraw upward and apart before approaching the figurine.
Move left above the figurine for a wrist-camera alignment check; return the empty right arm toward its home pose.
Lower the open left fingers toward the figurine's shoulders, with a small lateral alignment correction. Right arm stays clear.
Advance slightly around the figurine's torso, close fully, and test the grasp with a short vertical lift.
Figurine retention is uncertain and its base stayed near the table. Reopen, reach farther around the torso at lower height, and reclose.
Test the revised figurine grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the gripper fully closed and watching the base for clearance.
Figurine base is visibly lifted. Raise for clock clearance and begin carrying it toward the small stand with the left gripper closed.
Corrected rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Carry the figurine toward the stand at constant clearance height.
Figurine slipped but is upright just in front of its stand. Reorient the open left gripper for a vertical regrasp and a short final placement.
Replan after continuity rejection using smaller wrist increments and a lower, less folded approach. Figurine has toppled near the stand; prepare to recover it.
Approach the fallen figurine from above, rotating the open fingers to span its torso rather than its length.
After continuity interruption, lower the wrist and reduce translation/rotation increments to approach the fallen torso without overfolding.
Use a shallower wrist angle to reach the fallen torso without extending the shoulder farther; align finger closing direction across the body.
Lower the aligned fingers around the fallen figurine's midsection, close, and make a small retention-test lift.
Lift the regrasped figurine clear while retreating from the monitor and begin rotating its body upright; keep the grip closed.
The figurine was not retained. Reapproach its chest rather than the legs, using a lower, more forward open grasp.
Descend another four centimeters around the chest and close without rotating, so the fingers reach below the torso rather than above it.
Test torso retention with a straight six-centimeter lift and slight retreat before attempting to right the figurine.
The figurine again remained on the table. Open and descend substantially farther so the short fingertips surround the torso near table level.
Center the torso between the fingertips, close at the deeper grasp height, and make a small straight lift to test retention.
The figurine now visibly rises with the fingers. Lift and retreat while gradually rotating its head upward, maintaining the closed grasp.
Figurine is now upright but no longer securely held. Reopen and approach its upright torso for a short leftward transfer onto the stand.
Advance the fingers around the upright torso, close fully, and make a small vertical retention check without changing orientation.
Lift the upright figurine slowly and begin a small leftward transfer, preserving wrist orientation and checking that its base follows.
The shallow grasp slipped. Open and approach the lower torso substantially deeper, keeping the wrist orientation fixed and avoiding the monitor.
Close the deeper torso grasp, pause, and lift slightly leftward to check whether the whole figurine follows.
Figurine base is lifted. Carry it left toward the stand while gently reducing its lean, keeping the torso grip closed.
Keep the figurine over the stand and rotate its head upward about the combined horizontal axis, adding clearance for its base.
Figurine is more upright and visibly retained. Lower it toward the stand while shifting its base slightly left and forward, without further wrist rotation.
Lower toward the stand with a gradual yaw adjustment and rearward wrist repositioning to reduce wrist-joint strain; retain the closed grasp.
Relieve the wrist limit by gently reducing upward pitch while aligning the figurine base over the stand; pause to assess support before release.
The previous chunk executed nothing. First settle at the observed pose, then use smaller pitch corrections to recover continuity near the wrist limit.
Release the figurine at stand height and withdraw the open fingers backward and upward to inspect its resting position.
Figurine tipped after release near the stand. Clear it and approach the alarm clock from above, leaving the right arm parked.
Align the left wrist more vertically above the clock and move the open fingers toward its sides.
Lower the open fingers around the clock's side walls with a small centering correction, then close fully.
Lift the clock while retreating slightly from the drawer, keeping it closed in the fingers and checking visible retention.
Raise the retained clock above the drawer rim while moving left; tilt the wrist slightly to preserve reach margin.
Replan below the folding limit: advance the clock over the drawer lip with a slightly shallower wrist and modestly lower EE height.
Lower the wrist to recover elbow margin while tilting the retained clock forward over the tray; advance only in small increments.
No prior motion executed. Use submillimeter initial lowering and very small pitch changes to move away from the near-folded IK boundary.
With elbow margin restored, advance the clock farther onto the drawer top and slightly toward its center, keeping the grasp closed.
Settle the clock on the drawer top, release it, and withdraw the left hand backward to inspect stability.
Clock appears supported on the drawer top. Clear it and start orienting the left fingers for a vertical pinch of the drawer handle.
Lower in front of the drawer handle and finish rotating the gripper so its fingers close vertically across the handle.
Correct the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Seat and close around the drawer handle, then test with a short straight pull.
The drawer did not visibly follow the test pull. Reopen and seat the fingers deeper around the handle before reclosing.
Corrected rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Settle the handle grasp, then test a slow straight pull from the observed pose.
Adjust the drawer grasp slightly upward and use a narrower opening to avoid contacting the surrounding panel, then reclose on the handle.
The handle is centered between the fingers. Pause closed, then pull straight backward while watching for drawer motion.
The drawer remains shut. Change to a slightly downward handle approach so the finger pads can reach around it without the gripper body hitting the panel.
Corrected rejected tensor; no preceding motion occurred. Center the angled handle grasp, close, and test a short rearward pull.
Test the centered handle grasp with a longer straight pull, holding wrist orientation fixed and checking actual drawer movement.
The drawer did not open. Release the handle and withdraw both arms toward their origins to inspect the organized items without occlusion.
Complete the unobstructed return toward the left origin with both grippers open; inspect remaining figurine and keyboard alignment afterward.
The figurine remains fallen near its stand. Begin a new left-arm approach targeting its rigid base rather than the slipping torso grasp.
Advance toward the figurine base from above, gradually rotating the open fingers to pinch across the disk's thickness.
Complete the overhead base approach with open fingers, keeping the left wrist in its workspace and checking clearance near the stand.
Replan after the rejected suffix with small fixed-orientation increments; lower and center the fingers around the base disk.
